PMID:24340234.setting: Department of Neurosurgery, Aga Khan University (single institution), elective spinal arthrodesis
PMID:24340234.standard: Cross-matched to transfused (C/T) ratio compared with the optimal 2:1 reported in the literature

cycle1.result: 292 units of packed red cells cross-matched, 66 transfused (C/T ratio 4.4:1); 39 of 85 patients (45.88%) transfused. C/T 6.9:1 for degenerative disease and 23:1 for cervical spine.

PMID:24340234.intervention: Recommended a blood ordering schedule: two units for preoperative haemoglobin <9 g/dl, trauma, adult idiopathic scoliosis or more than two levels; group and hold for the rest. Not re-audited.

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:24340234.other_findings: On multivariate analysis only indication for surgery was independently associated with transfusion (AIS adjusted OR 124.87, trauma 34.37 versus degenerative disease).

PMID:41049922.setting: Trauma unit, district general hospital (University Hospitals Dorset, Poole)
PMID:41049922.standard: BOAST and radiographic positioning criteria for a true lateral ankle view (four criteria); target 100% for each

cycle1.result: Criterion 1 (fibula superimposed by posterior tibia) 83%; criterion 2 (talar domes superimposed) 61%; criterion 3 (open uniform tibiotalar joint) 69%; criterion 4 (landmarks included) 99%.

PMID:41049922.intervention: Posters in the emergency department and orthopaedic on-call room/radiography suites, and a teaching session by a foot and ankle associate specialist for orthopaedic staff and radiographers.

cycle2.result: Criterion 1 95% (p=0.0129); criterion 2 85% (p=0.0002); criterion 3 92% (p=0.0001); criterion 4 99% (p=1.0).

PMID:41049922.other_findings: Talar dome superimposition remained the hardest criterion to meet; the usual failure of criterion 4 was omission of the base of the fifth metatarsal.

PMID:36582572.topic: Preoperative medication administration when nil by mouth
PMID:36582572.setting: Trauma theatre list patients on orthopaedic/surgical wards, Basildon University Hospital
PMID:36582572.standard: Local and national (Royal College of Anaesthetists) guidance that preoperative trauma patients receive prescribed medications while nil by mouth, except anticoagulants, ACE inhibitors and ARBs

cycle1.result: 16/41 (39%) received their medications correctly; 22 critical drug class omissions; 19 omitted because nil by mouth.

PMID:36582572.intervention: Poster on drug trolleys listing which medications to give or withhold, meetings with ward managers and nursing staff, and presentation at orthopaedic and anaesthetic audit meetings.

cycle2.result: 25/41 (61%) received their medications correctly; 10 critical drug class omissions; 12 omitted because nil by mouth.

PMID:36582572.other_findings: Being nil by mouth was the main reason for omission; the abstract states 40 patients in the first round while the text gives 41.

PMID:26734297.setting: Orthopaedic department, James Paget University Hospital (district general hospital), elective and trauma lists
PMID:26734297.standard: Local standard from patient survey: a patient should be seen by the same surgeon from preoperative clinic to surgery and postoperative follow-up

cycle1.result: Same surgeon throughout 23%; same team 43%; operated on by clinic surgeon 50%; followed up by operating surgeon 40%; trauma continuity 10%.

PMID:26734297.intervention: Trauma on-call rota reorganised to weekly consultant 'on take' so the admitting team operates, and ward clerk booked follow-up into the operating surgeon's clinic.

cycle2.result: Same surgeon throughout 24%; same team 56%; operated on by clinic surgeon 60%; followed up by operating surgeon 43%; trauma same team 75%.

PMID:26734297.other_findings: A survey of 1000 outpatients found 92% wanted the same surgeon in clinic and theatre and 94% wanted follow-up by the operating surgeon. Individual surgeon continuity barely changed.

PMID:18817559.setting: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, University Hospital of Wales, Cardiff (teaching hospital), on-call handover
PMID:18817559.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England 'Safe Handover' minimum dataset and BMA guidance; gold standard 100% data transmission and 100% proforma compliance

cycle1.result: Handwritten plain paper sheets: patient labels used 73% (35/48); side of injury handed over in 28/49; tasks performed or outstanding 31% (15); relevant blood results 19% (6/32); overall data handed over 72.6%.

PMID:18817559.intervention: Standardised handover proforma based on the RCS dataset, piloted (version 1, 78% compliance), revised after junior doctor feedback and implemented as version 2.

cycle2.result: 100% proforma compliance; labels 96% (53/55); side of injury 98% (54/55); tasks 100% (55/55); relevant blood results 20% (6/29); overall data handed over 93.2% (p<0.01).

PMID:18817559.other_findings: Handover of relevant blood results stayed poor, possibly because the form had no dedicated field for it. The abstract reports label use as 72.9% to 93.4%.

PMID:40851711.setting: Trauma and orthopaedic department, King's Mill Hospital, Sherwood Forest Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust; inpatients aged 65+ with hip fracture
PMID:40851711.standard: NICE: cognitive assessment (AMTS or 4AT) within 24 hours of admission for hip fracture patients aged 65 and over, with regular postoperative assessment

cycle1.result: Admission AMTS within 24 hours 15 (78.9%); postoperative AMTS 18 (94.7%); postoperative 4AT 9 (47.4%); no postoperative delirium.

PMID:40851711.intervention: Educational posters with QR codes for AMTS and 4AT calculators on wards and doctors' office, and a staff training session for doctors.

cycle2.result: Admission AMTS 29 (96.7%); postoperative AMTS 26 (86.7%); postoperative 4AT 18 (60.0%); postoperative delirium 6 (20.0%).

PMID:40851711.other_findings: Postoperative 4AT documentation remained well below full compliance.

PMID:38149128.setting: Orthopaedic wards, University Hospital Lewisham (London teaching hospital), adult inpatients
PMID:38149128.standard: Trust treatment escalation plan (TEP) policy: TEP completed for emergency adult admissions, within 48 hours

cycle1.result: Overall TEP completion 69.5%; completed within 48 hours 47.82%; mean time to complete 4.4 days; mean overrides 3.2; longest 35 days; 24 instances of skipping. Incomplete TEPs 30.4% (n=7).

PMID:38149128.intervention: Revised local TEP pathway/algorithm allowing F1+ doctors to complete TEPs for young patients with simple fractures, algorithm displayed in trauma room, emails, individual teaching, and reminders to discuss TEP status on the post-take ward round.

cycle2.result: Overall completion 88.2%; completed within 48 hours 35.29%; mean time 3.7 days; mean overrides 1.3; longest 13 days; 5 instances of skipping. Incomplete TEPs 11.76% (n=2).

PMID:38149128.other_findings: Completion within 48 hours fell between cycles despite better overall completion. A junior doctor questionnaire found TEPs were skipped because of competing clinical priorities.

PMID:40772178.topic: Ottawa knee rules compliance in radiograph requests
PMID:40772178.setting: Emergency department and orthopaedic referrers, Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust (high-volume trauma centre)
PMID:40772178.standard: Ottawa Knee Rules (endorsed by NICE and RCR iRefer) documented in knee radiograph requests; target 100%

cycle1.result: At least one OKR criterion documented 41%; age >=55 52%; fibular head tenderness 3%; isolated patellar tenderness 13%; inability to flex to 90 degrees 3%; inability to bear weight 14%. Adequate documentation: orthopaedic SHOs/registrars 35.7%, ENPs/ANPs/triage 52.4%.

PMID:40772178.intervention: Posters and leaflets in clinical areas, presentations at departmental meetings, formal and informal teaching, and emails summarising the rules.

cycle2.result: At least one OKR criterion 91% (p<0.01); age 62%; fibular head tenderness 68%; patellar tenderness 72%; inability to flex 65%; inability to bear weight 57%. Adequate documentation: orthopaedic SHOs/registrars 92.9%, ENPs/ANPs/triage 88.2%.

PMID:40772178.other_findings: 9% of cycle 2 referrals still lacked adequate documentation; authors suggest OKR prompts in the electronic request system.

PMID:36465782.setting: Regional trauma and tertiary referral centre, Galway University Hospitals; acute orthopaedic trauma admissions
PMID:36465782.standard: Irish HSE Standards and Recommended Practices for Healthcare Records Management and HSE National Model of Care for Trauma and Orthopaedic Surgery documentation standards (checklist)

cycle1.result: Unscripted notes: consultant on call 78% (39/50); time of injury 72% (36/50); associated injury 48% (24/50); smoking status 86% (43/50); alcohol 42% (21/50); vital signs 28% (14/50); other systems 14% (7/50).

PMID:36465782.intervention: Standardised admission proforma developed with multidisciplinary stakeholders after results were presented at departmental teaching, with an accompanying education session; one-month introduction period.

cycle2.result: Proforma notes: consultant on call 100% (p=0.0005); time of injury 100% (p=0.0001); associated injury 100% (p=0.0001); smoking 100% (p=0.0001); alcohol 94% (p=0.0001); vital signs 70% (p=0.0001); other systems 74% (p=0.0001).

PMID:36465782.other_findings: Admitting doctor grade documentation fell from 92% to 82% and vital signs remained incomplete at 70%. A poll of 16 Irish units found admission proforma use in only 18.8%.

PMID:20721318.setting: Trauma and orthopaedic unit, St Helens and Knowsley Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (teaching hospital); records of the clinical audit department
PMID:20721318.standard: NICE principles for best practice in clinical audit: every audit should complete the cycle with re-audit (100%)

cycle1.result: Of 61 audits, 12 (19.7%) abandoned, 44 (72.1%) presented and 5 (8.2%) ongoing; audit cycle completed by re-audit in only 13 (29%).

PMID:20721318.intervention: Recommendations only (signed undertaking by audit lead, reallocation to a new trainee, email reminders of re-audit dates, consultant supervision); no re-audit reported.

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:20721318.other_findings: A consultant led or supervised 59% of audits; 7 of 12 abandoned audits had no reason recorded. Hip fracture was the commonest topic (19.7%).

PMID:26734446.topic: Baseline DEXA scanning in breast cancer
PMID:26734446.setting: Russells Hall Hospital, Dudley (district general hospital); newly diagnosed breast cancer
PMID:26734446.standard: NICE guideline 80: baseline DEXA for early invasive breast cancer starting aromatase inhibitors, with treatment-induced menopause or starting ovarian ablation/suppression; target 100%

cycle1.result: 100 patients sampled, 66 with early/locally invasive cancer, 42 with an indication; 16/42 (38%) had a DEXA scan. Of those scanned 8/16 (50%) osteopaenic and 1/16 (6%) osteoporotic.

PMID:26734446.intervention: Results presented to surgical and oncology departments and the breast MDT, posters summarising the guideline in breast clinics and MDT areas, and MDT discussion of the need for DEXA.

cycle2.result: 11/11 (100%) indicated patients received a DEXA scan (17 early breast cancers).

PMID:26734446.other_findings: Earlier re-audits: January 2014 9/10 (90%) and February 2014 12/13 (92%). 16% of records were incomplete and excluded.

PMID:40918921.topic: VTE prophylaxis after non-arthroplasty knee surgery
PMID:40918921.setting: Joint replacement unit, tertiary orthopaedic hospital (University Hospitals Dorset / Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital affiliations); elective non-arthroplasty knee procedures
PMID:40918921.standard: NICE VTE guidance: prophylaxis after arthroscopy if anaesthetic time 90 minutes or more (or VTE risk outweighs bleeding risk), and after all other non-arthroplasty knee surgery; target 100%

cycle1.result: Arthroscopy with anaesthetic time >90 minutes 2/4 (50%) received prophylaxis; other non-arthroplasty surgery 9/25 (36%).

PMID:40918921.intervention: Formal teaching session for the joint replacement unit team by a senior consultant on recording anaesthetic time, weight-bearing status and VTE prescription on operation notes and postoperative instructions.

cycle2.result: Arthroscopy >90 minutes 6/11 (55%) (p=1.0); other non-arthroplasty surgery 27/40 (68%) (p=0.02).

PMID:40918921.other_findings: No VTE events were reported. The text states both 56 and 66 patients for the second loop; authors suggest a VTE checklist with discharge summaries.

PMID:39835043.topic: Tranexamic acid use in knee arthroplasty
PMID:39835043.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics Department, Good Hope Hospital, University Hospitals Birmingham (elective surgical hub)
PMID:39835043.standard: NICE: combined topical and intravenous tranexamic acid in knee arthroplasty for patients without renal impairment (1 g IV only with significant renal impairment)

cycle1.result: TXA used in 20 (48.8%), not used in 21 (51.2%); combined IV and topical 3 (7.3%); IV only 14 (34.1%); topical only 3 (7.3%).

PMID:39835043.intervention: Targeted emails to consultants and registrars, presentation at a specialty meeting, and posters on TXA and NICE guidance on computers across the elective surgical suite.

cycle2.result: TXA used in 38 (73.1%) (p=0.016), not used in 14 (26.9%); combined IV and topical 16 (30.8%) (p=0.005); IV only 22 (42.3%).

PMID:39835043.other_findings: In cycle 2 non-use was 20% (8/40) without a tourniquet versus 50% (6/12) with one. In significant renal impairment TXA was omitted in 8/9 (cycle 1) and 6/12 (cycle 2).

PMID:40755948.setting: Trauma orthopaedic unit, Salford Care Organisation (Northern Care Alliance NHS hospital); adult trauma surgery
PMID:40755948.standard: Northern Care Alliance 2023 orthopaedic antibiotic prophylaxis guideline (choice, timing within 60 minutes, duration) and NICE NG180 (blood pressure within 20% of baseline, core temperature 36.5-37.5°C); 100% target for timing and blood pressure

cycle1.result: Correct intraoperative antibiotic 68/104 (65.4%); given within 60 minutes 104/104 (100%); postoperative duration compliant 67/104 (64.4%); overuse 25/104 (24%); blood pressure within target 104/104 (100%); temperature documented 36/104 (35%).

PMID:40755948.intervention: Planned: EPR alerts for antibiotic choice and duration, mandatory temperature documentation fields, staff education and a compliance dashboard; re-audit planned in six months.

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:40755948.other_findings: Postoperative compliance was lowest in joint replacement (40%, overuse 37%) and best in internal fixation (75%); all documented temperatures were normothermic.

PMID:40688888.topic: VTE prophylaxis after hip and knee arthroplasty
PMID:40688888.setting: Russells Hall Hospital, Dudley (district general hospital); elective total hip and knee replacement discharge summaries
PMID:40688888.standard: NICE VTE guidance: THR 28 days LMWH plus anti-embolism stockings until discharge; TKR 14 days LMWH plus stockings

cycle1.result: THR 23/25 (92%) and TKR 20/23 (87%) received enoxaparin plus stockings; overall compliance 90%.

PMID:40688888.intervention: Arthroplasty discharge pack displayed as posters and handouts at the arthroplasty station, regular teaching sessions on NICE discharge guidance, and final check of discharge letters by the nurse in charge.

cycle2.result: THR 24/24 (100%) and TKR 22/23 (96%) correct; overall compliance 98%.

PMID:40688888.other_findings: Overall compliance was calculated as the average of the THR and TKR rates; patient outcomes were not recorded.

PMID:21943077.setting: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Sunderland Royal Hospital (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: 29 patients had preoperative echo versus 40 random non-echo controls (from 349 hip fractures). Mean delay to surgery 2.7 days (range 0-6) with echo versus 1.1 days (range 0-3) without (p<0.001); no difference in length of stay (16.7 vs 15.4 days, p=0.14) or 30-day mortality (p=0.41).

PMID:21943077.intervention: Departmental guidelines for expediting echo requests in hip fracture patients with a murmur and a liaison with cardiology to prioritise them; no re-audit reported.

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:21943077.other_findings: No patient needed preoperative cardiac intervention; 14 had an aortic valve abnormality including 2 severe and 1 critical aortic stenosis, and 10% had no valvular pathology.

PMID:38699119.setting: Urgent treatment centre and emergency departments of two district general hospitals
PMID:38699119.standard: AO Foundation guidance: ankle immobilised in neutral plantigrade position; acceptable tibia-to-sole angle 80-100 degrees on lateral radiograph

cycle1.result: Mean angle 108.5 degrees (SD 11.7); 18/65 (27.7%) within 80-100 degrees (DGH 1 n=32, DGH 2 n=33).

PMID:38699119.intervention: Single interactive session led by plaster technicians (for UTC nurses at DGH 1 and for ED junior doctors at DGH 2) plus educational posters where plastering occurred.

cycle2.result: Mean angle 106.2 degrees (SD 11.9) (p=0.285); 23/61 (37.7%) within 80-100 degrees (p=0.231) (DGH 1 n=28, DGH 2 n=33).

PMID:38699119.other_findings: Acceptable casts improved by 22% at the site that trained UTC nurses but only 3% at the site that trained junior doctors; angles were measured by a single reviewer.

PMID:16759384.setting: Tibetan Delek Hospital, Dharamsala (small general hospital without on-site obstetricians); all labour admissions
PMID:16759384.standard: Hospital policy of active management of the third stage of labour; WHO partogram use for labour management and transfer decisions

cycle1.result: Postpartum haemorrhage 7 (12%); retained placenta 3 (5%); 11 (19%) transferred, 8 (75%) for 'failure to progress' in uncomplicated primiparous women; no partograms used.

PMID:16759384.intervention: Staff retraining in active management of the third stage with intramuscular Syntometrine at delivery of the anterior shoulder, introduction of the WHO partogram with training, and feedback seminars, one-to-one sessions and newsletter reports after each cycle.

cycle2.result: PPH 5 (6%); retained placenta 0; 6 (7%) transferred, 1 (17%) for failure to progress; partograms used in 77 (86%), complete and accurate in 13 (17%).

PMID:16759384.other_findings: Interim audits: 1997 (n=110) PPH 6%, partogram use 80% with 30% unhelpful; 1998 (n=65) PPH 5%, partogram use 87% with 60% complete. Partogram quality declined by 2003 after staff turnover.

PMID:40263145.topic: Vertebral fragility fracture reporting on CT
PMID:40263145.setting: UK-wide Royal College of Radiologists national audit with the Royal Osteoporosis Society and Royal College of Physicians; radiology departments
PMID:40263145.standard: RCR national audit of reporting vertebral fragility fractures (Genant grading) on non-trauma CT including the thoracolumbar spine in patients over 70

cycle1.result: Moderate/severe vertebral fragility fractures reported in 26%.

PMID:40263145.intervention: A series of UK-wide interventions between audits (details not given in the abstract).

cycle2.result: Moderate/severe vertebral fragility fractures reported in 32%; VFF incidence 21.7%; improvements across all patient-related and organisational parameters.

PMID:40263145.other_findings: Each site reviewed 50-100 consecutive CT studies. Modelling predicts 23,420 extra diagnoses, 562 hip fractures prevented in year one with treatment and a potential saving of £13,207,000.

EPMC:PMC:PMC9383793.topic: Bone protection after fragility fracture in the very elderly
EPMC:PMC:PMC9383793.setting: North Staffordshire Fracture Liaison Service; patients aged 85 and over with fragility fracture, GP prescribing
EPMC:PMC:PMC9383793.standard: FLS policy in line with national guidance: GP letter advising empirical oral bisphosphonate for patients aged 85 and over after fragility fracture

cycle1.dates: Fractures December 2018 to October 2020; data collected October 2020
cycle1.result: 160/396 (40%) prescribed a bisphosphonate (median 9 months after fracture); over 90% alendronic acid.

EPMC:PMC:PMC9383793.intervention: Standard GP letter rewritten using GP feedback to address barriers, including advice on relative contraindications and referral.

cycle2.dates: Fractures December 2020 to May 2021; data collected July 2021
cycle2.result: 38/74 (51%) prescribed a bisphosphonate (median 5 months after fracture).

EPMC:PMC:PMC9383793.other_findings: 408 eligible patients in cycle 1, with Summary Care Record data for 396. Different fracture-to-audit intervals between cycles limit comparison.
